title: Advances in understanding contact electrification via DFT and molecular dynamics simulations
abstract: Contact electrification (CE) has been studied for many years, yet its mechanism remains unclear and theories are inconsistent. This Review discusses experimental and theoretical studies on CE, highlighting how CE may be dominated by the competition and coupling among electron transfer, ion transfer and material transfer between two surfaces under different conditions. These transfer mechanisms have been found experimentally, but their quantitative impact on CE has not yet been determined owing to the limited spatial and temporal resolution of instruments. Fortunately, density functional theory and molecular dynamics yield the possibility of solving this obstacle. Electron transfer is driven by work function changes or frontier orbital matching, and it is regulated by strain-induced electronic state restructuring and the flexoelectric effect. Ion transfer is promoted by the formation of capillary water bridges and is regulated by the disruption of hydrogen-bond networks in the interfacial water layer, and material transfer arises from mechanical stress. Lastly, we highlight future work hat is important for further studies of CE.

title: Dynamic interactions at active sites in electrocatalysis
abstract: The dynamic evolution of heterogeneous electrocatalysts under operating conditions underscores the importance of how the multiple components of catalytic reactions interact. These parts interact dynamically to define the active sites, making it essential yet challenging to assign their mechanistic roles during electrocatalysis. By exploring advances in the dynamic evolution of electrocatalysts from the perspective of interfacial dynamics, this Review systematically examines the key participants composing dynamic active sites and classifies their interactions into: active centre–active centre, active centre–functional motif, active centre–intermediate, and active centre–microenvironment interactions. Furthermore, it provides details on how these interactions become entangled into higher-order interactive dynamics; their spatiotemporal resolution through complementary operando and theoretical approaches; and how controlling them can guide catalyst design. Moreover, the central challenges and future opportunities are outlined for establishing a more complete understanding of the dynamic interactions within the active sites of electrocatalytic systems.
